Israel multiplied greatly in Egypt. How was God keeping his promise to Abraham?
A new king oppressed the Israelites, but the more they were oppressed, the more they multiplied. What does this show about God's purposes?
The midwives feared God and would not kill the babies. Where might fearing God mean saying no to people in power?
Moses' mother hid him and trusted God with his life. What does her courage teach you?
Moses tried to bring justice in his own way and had to flee. What happens when we act in our own strength?
Moses helped the women at the well. How can you stand up for those treated unfairly?
God heard their groaning and remembered his covenant. What does it mean that God hears your cries?
God spoke from the burning bush: "Take off your sandals, for the place you are standing is holy ground." What does God's holiness mean to you?
God says, "I have seen the affliction of my people... I know their sufferings." How does this comfort you?
Moses asked, "Who am I?" and God said, "I will be with you." Where do you need this answer?
God revealed his name: "I AM WHO I AM." What does this name tell you about God?
God gave Moses signs to show he was sent by God. What does this show about God's power?
Moses said he was not eloquent, and God said, "I will be with your mouth." What excuse might you be giving God?
The people believed and bowed and worshipped when they heard God had seen their affliction. How do you respond to God's care?
Pharaoh said, "Who is the Lord, that I should obey his voice?" How do people today ask the same?
Things got worse after Moses obeyed God. How do you hold on when obedience seems to make things harder?
Moses brought his complaint honestly to God. How can you bring your honest questions to God?
God promised, "I will bring you out... I will redeem you... I will take you to be my people." Which promise speaks to you?
The people could not listen because of their broken spirit. How do you encourage someone who is too discouraged to hope?
Moses still felt inadequate. How does God work through people who feel weak?
God says the Egyptians would know that he is the Lord. What does God want the world to know about him?
Aaron's staff swallowed the magicians' staffs. What does this show about God's power over false gods?
The Nile was turned to blood, yet Pharaoh hardened his heart. Why do people resist God even in the face of his power?
Pharaoh begged for relief from the frogs but hardened his heart once relief came. When do we turn to God only in trouble?
The magicians said, "This is the finger of God." What makes people recognise God's hand?
God made a distinction between his people and Egypt. What does it mean to be set apart by God?
God protected Israel's livestock. How has God protected what is yours?
Some Egyptians who feared the word of the Lord brought their servants in. What does this show about listening to God's warnings?
Pharaoh said, "I have sinned," but did not change. What is the difference between regret and repentance?
God says the plagues are so you may tell your children what he has done. What story of God would you tell the next generation?
Pharaoh's servants begged him to let the people go. Why is it so hard for a proud heart to give in?
There was darkness in Egypt, but light where Israel lived. How does God's light shine in dark times?
The Lord gave the people favour in the sight of the Egyptians. How has God given you favour?
God makes a distinction between Egypt and Israel. What does this show about God's protection of his people?
Pharaoh still would not listen. What does this teach about hardened hearts?
When God saw the blood of the lamb, he passed over. How does this point to Jesus, the Lamb of God?
The Passover was to be a lasting memorial. Why does God want his people to remember?
The people bowed and worshipped when they heard God's instructions. How do you respond to God's saving plan?
It was a night of watching by the Lord. What does it mean that God keeps watch over his people?
Moses said, "Remember this day, in which you came out from Egypt." What saving work of God do you need to remember?
Children would ask, "What does this mean?" How can you explain what God has done to the next generation?
God led them by a pillar of cloud by day and fire by night. How does God guide you today?
God led Israel to a place where they seemed trapped. Why might God lead you into difficult places?
"The Lord will fight for you, and you have only to be silent." Where do you need to trust God to fight for you?
God made a way through the sea. When has God made a way where there seemed to be none?
The people feared the Lord and believed in him. How has seeing God's work strengthened your faith?
"The Lord is my strength and my song, and he has become my salvation." How has God been your strength and song?
"Who is like you, O Lord?" What makes God unlike anyone else?
The people grumbled at bitter water, and God made it sweet. What bitter situation do you need God to sweeten?
After Marah came Elim, with springs and palm trees. How has God brought refreshment after hardship?
The people grumbled and wished they were back in Egypt. When are you tempted to look back?
God rained bread from heaven every morning. How does God provide your daily bread?
Manna gathered beyond what was needed went bad. What does this teach about trusting God day by day?
God gave a double portion so they could rest. How does God care for our rest?
The people asked, "Is the Lord among us or not?" When have you asked that?
Israel prevailed while Moses' hands were held up. Who holds your arms up, and whose can you hold up?
Moses built an altar and called it "The Lord is my banner." What does it mean for God to be your banner?
Jethro rejoiced when he heard all the good the Lord had done. Who could you tell about God's goodness?
Jethro told Moses, "What you are doing is not good... you cannot do it alone." Where do you need to share the load?
Moses listened to his father-in-law's advice. How open are you to wise counsel?
God said, "I bore you on eagles' wings and brought you to myself." What does this picture tell you about God's care?
God calls his people a treasured possession and a kingdom of priests. What does this mean for you?
The people prepared themselves to meet a holy God. How do you prepare your heart to meet God?
God begins the commandments by reminding them he brought them out of slavery. Why does he start there?
Which of the first four commandments, about loving God, challenges you most?
Which of the commandments about loving others do you need to pay attention to?
Moses said God had come to test them so the fear of him may keep them from sinning. What does healthy fear of God look like?
God's law limited and protected even servants. What does this show about God's concern for the vulnerable?
God's laws took harm against others seriously. Why does God care so much about how we treat each other?
People were responsible for harm caused by what they owned. How can you take responsibility for your possessions and actions?
God required people to make things right when they caused loss. Is there anything you need to make right?
God says not to wrong the sojourner, widow or orphan, for he hears their cry. Who are the vulnerable around you?
God says, "If he cries to me, I will hear, for I am compassionate." What does this show about God?
God calls for honesty and fairness, even to your enemy. How can you treat fairly someone you dislike?
God gives rest to the land, the poor and even the animals. What does this teach about rest?
God promises to send an angel before them. How has God gone before you?
The people said, "All the words the Lord has spoken we will do." What would it mean to say that today?
The leaders saw God and ate and drank. What does this show about the fellowship God offers?
Moses waited on the mountain for six days before God spoke. How can you wait on God?
God asked for offerings from everyone whose heart moved them. What does it mean to give with a willing heart?
God said, "Let them make me a sanctuary, that I may dwell in their midst." What does God's desire to dwell with us show?
God would meet with Moses above the mercy seat. What does it mean that God meets us at the place of mercy?
Every detail of the tabernacle was given by God. What does this show about how God wants to be approached?
A veil separated the Most Holy Place. How does Jesus open the way to God?
The altar stood at the entrance of the courtyard. Why did sacrifice come first?
The lamp was to burn continually before the Lord. What keeps the light of faith burning in your life?
Aaron's garments were "for glory and for beauty." What does this show about serving God?
The priest carried the names of the tribes on his shoulders before the Lord. How does Jesus carry you before the Father?
The names were also on the breastpiece over his heart. What does it mean that you are on Jesus' heart?
The plate read "Holy to the Lord." What would it mean for your life to be marked this way?
The priests were washed, clothed and anointed. How does this picture what God does for us in Christ?
There was to be a daily offering morning and evening. How do you begin and end your day with God?
God says, "I will dwell among the people of Israel and will be their God." What does God's presence mean to you?
Incense was to rise before the Lord every day. How is prayer like incense?
Everyone, rich or poor, gave the same ransom. What does this show about how God sees us?
The priests had to wash before serving. What does it mean to come to God cleansed?
God filled Bezalel with his Spirit for skilled craftsmanship. How can your skills and work serve God?
The Sabbath was a sign that God sanctifies his people. How can rest remind you of God's work in you?
The law was written by the finger of God. What does this tell you about God's word?
The people made a golden calf while waiting for Moses. What do we turn to when God seems slow?
Moses pleaded for the people, and the Lord relented. What does this teach about intercession?
Aaron made excuses: "Out came this calf." How do we excuse our sins?
Moses offered to be blotted out for the people. How does this point to Jesus?
The people mourned when God said he would not go with them. How much do you value God's presence?
The Lord spoke to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend. What does friendship with God look like?
Moses said, "If your presence will not go with me, do not bring us up from here." Why is God's presence what matters most?
Moses prayed, "Please show me your glory." What would you ask to see of God?
God proclaimed himself "merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love." Which of these do you need most?
Moses quickly bowed and worshipped. How do you respond when you see God's character?
God warned them against making covenants that would lead them to idols. What relationships pull you from God?
Moses' face shone after being with God. How does time with God change you?
Whoever was of a generous heart brought an offering. How can you give generously?
Everyone whose heart stirred him and whose spirit moved him came. What is stirring your heart to give or serve?
God filled craftsmen with skill and the ability to teach. How can you use your skills for God?
Everyone whom the Lord had given skill came to do the work. What has God equipped you to do?
The people brought more than enough, so they had to be told to stop. What would generosity like this look like today?
The work was done carefully, exactly as God commanded. How can you do your work with care and faithfulness?
Bezalel made the ark with the mercy seat and cherubim. What does the mercy seat remind you of?
The table and lampstand were made of gold. What does this show about the beauty of worship?
The altar of incense and the anointing oil were carefully made. What does this teach about prayer and holiness?
The altar of burnt offering stood at the entrance. Why is sacrifice at the heart of approaching God?
The bronze basin was made from the mirrors of the women who served. What does their gift show?
Every gift was counted carefully. What does this teach about faithful stewardship?
The garments were made "as the Lord had commanded Moses." Why does careful obedience matter?
The holy crown read "Holy to the Lord." How can your life display holiness?
Moses saw all the work and blessed them. How does God see your faithful work?
God told Moses to set up the tabernacle on the first day of the first month. What new beginning might God be giving you?
Moses did everything just as the Lord commanded. How can you follow God carefully?
The glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle. What does it mean that God's glory came to dwell with his people?
